newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Feb 26 - There were no suprises from latest official palm oil figures released by PORLA last Saturday February 22. CPO production fell 9.6 percent or 61,100 tonnes to 577,000 tonnes in January. Production in Peninsular Malaysia was down 11 percent against our estimate of a drop more than 12 percent. As expected, East Malaysia fared better with a decline of 5.9 percent. On an annual basis, production in the country expanded slightly by 1.9 percent.

A contraction of 7.8 percent or 35,000 tonnes in Peninsular Malaysia was fully offset by a robust growth of 38.2 percent or 45,600 tonnes in East Malaysia. This divergence in growth is expected to continue into February. Partial data for first-half February show production declines ranged widely from down 25-50 percent when compared to first-half January. Bigger declines were recorded by producers/millers whose workers took more days off during the Chinese New Year and Hari Raya holidays. Harvesters/mills had started to clear the backlog since late last week.

At the moment it is uncertain whether the backlog could be fully cleared by the end of this month as some producing areas, especially those in Sabah and Sarawak, had widespread rains for several days. Tentatively we expect production in the country this month to post a seasonal decline of around 21 percent or 122,000 tonnes. Palm oil stocks at end January shrank 98,200 tonnes to 696,300 tonnes or somewhat below our estimate of 715,000 tonnes. Stocks of CPO alone fell 79,400 tonnes to 356,100 tonnes. The entire decline was recorded by Peninsular Malaysia which reduced its stocks by 83,000 tonnes.

Compared to year ago, CPO stocks in the country were drawn down considerably by 138,600 tonnes. Stocks of palm oil are likely to be further rundown by some 100,000 tonnes to around 595,000 tonnes at the end of this month. Stocks of CPO alone could be depleted to as low as 270,000 tonnes as against 407,000 tonnes at end February 1996. PORLA reported palm oil exports fell to 551,700 tonnes in January from 652,900 tonnes (revised) in December. Tight supplies and poor margins for refineries would curtail exports further this month, possibly to 465-470,000 tonnes.

Improved supplies in March are however likely to result in a strong recovery in shipments. A slackening off in shortcovering to easier price tendencies in recent days. Speculation on India raising its import duty on palm oil from 20 percent to 30 percent had also resulted in some buyers staying on the sideline. This does not look likely as the Indian Prime Minister had just announced price subsidies for staple food items like rice and wheat for some 320 million Indians whose income fall below the poverty line.
April and May CPO futures settled at 1,278 ringgit and 1,268 ringgit respectively yesterday, down from 1,317 ringgit and 1,304 ringgit a week ago.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
